findings.reason: the plan must hand §10's dotfiles half to the coordinator the way §11 step 2 does for router deployment, or the node cannot be dispatched to a worker and cannot close.
findings.text: §10 requires edits inside dotfiles (`_gpu_sample.py` deleted at line 541, `bin/gpu-watch` reduced to a launcher here) while §11 line 563 says "Any worker node can build them" and the plan's own `watch-home` decision records that workers cannot write dotfiles, so a dispatched §10 node stops at the write fence

findings.reason: naming the composer's home, and that it supersedes `_publish_lane`, is what prevents the two-writers-to-one-path defect this section exists to fix.
findings.text: §5 introduces "one composer" that writes every pool document but names no function or file for it, while §1 line 56 records the defect as `RouterApp._publish_lane` reading `upstreams[0]`; nothing states that the composer replaces that publisher, so a worker can leave `_publish_lane` in place and add a second writer to `lane.json`

findings.reason: a worker implementing §9 exactly is blocked, and the plan would need to name a fixture whose viewer account holds more than six projects.
findings.text: §9's golden requires the viewer's per-project table to show "at most six project rows and a `+N more` row" rendered from "the two-account fixture from §8", but that fixture (line 397) carries three projects in total, so the `+N more` row cannot appear and the gate cannot pass as written
